strengths.home: Winless in three UNL games (D2, L1) after conceding an 85th-minute equaliser to Austria, but won two of their last three at home and three of the last four UNL home games. Vedat Muriqi scored the winner in their only victory; Lumbardh Dellova is out.
strengths.away: Israel: winless this campaign (D2, L2) after drawing 1-1 with Ireland, and promotion hopes rest on other results. Manor Solomon has helped them win each of the seven internationals he has scored in; only one of their last 12 goals came in the first half.

vyCbg1Ta.synopsis: A cagey contest where Kosovo can secure League B with a win and Israel risk the play-offs. Both sides have scored little recently, and Flashscore's writer points to under 2.5 goals.

strengths.home: AFC Wimbledon: 18th with 13 points, four defeats in their last five and just 0.6 goals a game over that spell; their xG of 1.0 and 2.7 shots on target a game are the worst in the league. Dujuan Richards is a doubt; Jayden Stockley has six goals.
strengths.away: Blackpool: 19th with 12 points, one win in their last five and a leaky defence (xG conceded 1.97, 6.2 shots on target faced a game), though their big-chance conversion of 52% is the best in the league. Josh Bowler has two goals and two assists; Josh Earl and CJ Hamilton are out.

G8iGPRhJ.synopsis: A relegation-zone meeting between two struggling sides, with Wimbledon's attack the weakest in the division and Blackpool's defence among the worst. Flashscore's stats preview names no pick.

strengths.home: MK Dons: 12th, four wins from their last five including a 6-1 home win over Doncaster, scoring 2.6 a game in that run; xG 1.78 a game. Aaron Collins leads the league with 13 goals; Ryan Barnett is a doubt.
strengths.away: Burton: 15th, one win in five and beaten 2-0 at Wycombe, scoring just 0.8 a game; they create the fewest big chances in the league (1.2 a game) and have made eight errors leading to goals. Caylan Vickers has one goal and four assists.

6uVex5xP.synopsis: MK Dons are in much better form and have the league's top scorer, against a Burton attack that struggles to create chances. Flashscore's stats preview names no pick.

strengths.home: Sheffield Wednesday: ninth, one win in five (two draws, two defeats) but good attacking numbers (xG 1.72, 5.5 shots on target a game). Jamal Lowe has five goals; Sil Swinkels is suspended and Joe Lumley is out, with Liam Cooper and Louie Barry doubts.
strengths.away: Plymouth: fifth with 23 points, two wins in their last five and a 0-0 draw with Reading last time, scoring 1.0 a game recently. xG of 1.52 and 1.47 conceded, about league average.

UH8Dfnhg.synopsis: Two mid-to-upper table sides with similar numbers and a few absences at Hillsborough. Flashscore's stats preview names no pick.

strengths.home: Stockport County: second with 26 points, three wins in their last five and the league's best xG (2.17 a game), most shots (17.2) and duel win rate (55%). Kyle Wootton has nine goals; Adama Sidibeh is unavailable.
strengths.away: Reading: sixth with 22 points, two wins in five but only 0.6 goals a game recently and beaten 2-0 by Oxford last time. Jack Marriott leads the scoring with eight goals and Kyreece Lisbie has five goals and four assists; Paudie O'Connor is suspended.

ruFTj4iI.synopsis: Stockport are the stronger side on underlying numbers and at home, while Reading's goals have dried up lately. Flashscore's stats preview names no pick.

strengths.home: Wigan: 21st with 11 points and a 11-22 goal record; one win in five, though they scored 1.0 a game in that run. The worst big-chance conversion in the league (23%). Dara Costelloe is a doubt and Luke Harris is out.
strengths.away: Barnsley: 23rd with nine points, one draw and four defeats in their last five and conceding 2.0 a game, but they create plenty (29.5 touches in the opposition box a game against Wigan's 19.4). Vimal Yoganathan has three goals in six; Jack Shepherd is suspended.

ERy1Yeyi.synopsis: A bottom-three clash between two sides who rarely win, with Barnsley creating more but defending poorly. Flashscore's stats preview names no pick.

strengths.home: Norway: bottom of the group after three straight defeats, though unbeaten at home in competitive games since March 2024 bar one defeat (W11, D3), with eight first-half goals in four UNL games. Oscar Bobb is a rising threat; no fresh absences.
strengths.away: Wales: level on three points, beat Norway 2-1 in the reverse fixture but lost to Denmark since and have won one of ten UNL games in the top tier. Failed to score in several recent games and are without Kieffer Moore, Jordan James and Dylan Lawlor.

SYw37rNa.synopsis: Norway are the clear favourites at home against a Wales side with injuries and a poor away record. Flashscore's writer picks Norway to win without conceding.

strengths.home: Georgia: goalless and bottom with two points, winless in eight competitive games and failing to score in six of those, and without star player Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (knee injury). Four of their last five wins came at home; Georges Mikautadze has nine goals in 14 caps.
strengths.away: Hungary: one point off the group lead (W2, D1, L1), with Barnabás Varga scoring eight in his last eight internationals. Without Loïc Négo; only three of their last eight internationals saw both teams score.

EwECQBgd.synopsis: Hungary arrive in far better form against a Georgia side that cannot score. Flashscore's writer backs Hungary to win and keep a clean sheet.

strengths.home: Austria: group leaders, unbeaten in 16 home games (W13, D3) and five straight home wins, and a win guarantees promotion; Michael Gregoritsch has scored five of his last seven goals at home. Carney Chukwuemeka and Marco Grüll are out.
strengths.away: Ireland: lost only one of four UNL games (W1, D2) and Troy Parrott has ten goals in his last ten international games, including a brace against Austria last month. James Abankwah is suspended.

n1F6iubC.synopsis: A promotion-chasing group B3 clash where a point would probably suit both sides. Flashscore's writer leans towards another draw, citing recent head-to-head history.

strengths.home: Northern Ireland: unbeaten group leaders (W2, D2), the only side yet to concede in the cycle, with one defeat in their last 11 at Windsor Park (W7, D3) and none of their last nine games seeing both teams score. Shea Charles is a key player; Ceadach O'Neill has withdrawn.
strengths.away: Ukraine: playing home games away from home because of the war, beaten in their last two in Slovakia and well short of the League A hopes; only one of their seven 2026 internationals was won by the home side. Vladyslav Vanat scores early for his club.

b31hwkw2.synopsis: Northern Ireland have momentum and a strong home record, with Ukraine unsettled. Flashscore's writer backs Northern Ireland to win.

strengths.home: Portugal: four wins from four, group top spot at stake, and 14 competitive home games unbeaten, though three wins were by one goal. First match since Cristiano Ronaldo retired; Gonçalo Ramos has scored in three straight. João Cancelo and Francisco Conceição are suspended, and Tomás Araújo, Nuno Tavares and Rafael Leão are out.
strengths.away: Denmark: two wins in three after losing 3-2 to Norway, but defensively inconsistent (seven conceded in the group), and seven of their last ten competitive games produced over 3.5 goals. Rasmus Højlund has scored in three of four.

tv3rrSgl.synopsis: Portugal are favoured at home, though Denmark can score and concede. Flashscore's writer picks a goals market, backing over 3.5 goals.

strengths.home: Romania: lost all four UNL games, trailing at half-time in each, and six of eight internationals in 2026. Răzvan Marin is suspended and Ionuț Radu is out; Alexandru Cicâldău has scored eight of his last nine goals after half-time.
strengths.away: Poland: one win in seven internationals (a 6-0 over Romania), but Robert Lewandowski has scored eight in his last three meetings with Romania, including two hat-tricks. Jan Bednarek is suspended.

YejRGeRN.synopsis: Poland have the better head-to-head record and Romania keep falling behind early. Flashscore's writer picks Poland to lead at half-time, a first-half market rather than a full-time result.

strengths.home: Sweden: unbeaten group leaders (W3, D1), eleven UNL games unbeaten, five straight home wins scoring 2+ each time, and a goal inside 20 minutes in five of their last six UNL games. Viktor Gyökeres has scored their last three goals; Besfort Zeneli withdrew.
strengths.away: Bosnia-Herzegovina: unbeaten and the only side to stop Sweden winning in this campaign, beat Poland 1-0 last time, and four of their last five internationals had under 2.5 goals. Ivan Bašić scored against Poland.

focWCnQk.synopsis: The unbeaten leaders at home against the only team to hold them. Flashscore's writer picks a home goal inside the opening 20 minutes, a goal-timing market rather than a result.
